evidence: world.loadScene(path, spawnName) registered through the neutral layer; it only queues (last request wins) - AppSceneServices.runPendingSceneTransfer executes at the frame-end structural flush, never inline (a switch stops every script)

the transfer keeps the play session: app state, UI host and the Persist table are untouched; it is waitIdle -> onStop (old scene) -> SceneManager::loadScene -> placePlayerAtSpawn, NOT stopRuntime (which would end play in the editor and wipe Persist)

Persist = LuaScriptingSystem::persistentState(), bound as the global at state build; only stopRuntime/stopSimulation swap in a fresh table (play-session exit), so chest flags survive transfers and never leak across plays
placePlayerAtSpawn: the scene's "Player" entity lands on the named root-level spawn marker (x/y only, actor keeps its z); missing marker or player logs and leaves the scene as authored

walkable-event protocol: Player.lua blocks on isSolid OR (occupant whose call("blocksEntry") ~= false) - doors answer false, chests/NPC default solid; stepping onto a cell pokes entityAt(x, y, self.entity) with onPlayerEnter

fixture: Content/Scenes/TownLarge.scene.json (64x64, Ground 4096 / Decor 776 / Overlay 241 cells, 20 NPCs + player = 5120 tile candidates + 21 sprite candidates), generated deterministically by Tools/make_scale_scene.py (--size/--npcs/--out for other sizes)
method: profile build + runtime CPU trace via --cpu-profile; frame root 'iterate' (600 frames, skip 60); analyzer .agent/plan/rpg-prototype/measure_trace.py; full record in r4-measurements.md

measured: recordFamily (the sprite-pass submission lives here) fits 1.14ms + 1.23us/candidate (700->1.77, 1329->3.05, 5134->7.41); TownLarge frame 10.56ms (95fps), so ~6.3ms of it is per-candidate CPU recording
measured: window 1024x768 -> 512x384 cuts the frame 7% with recordFamily unchanged and Render/Frame self -0.84ms -> the bottleneck is per-candidate CPU, not fill
measured: whole-map extraction 0.10-0.15ms at 5134 candidates (~1/50 of the submission cost); Lua 0.015-0.04ms
decision 1: batching / instancing is needed and is the highest-value render change (the one cost that grows linearly with content; only 2 distinct textures here)
decision 2: the 16-entry texture table is not the binding constraint (2 used), but its per-frame rebuild + per-candidate linear scan should become a direct mapping with batching
decision 3: bypassing Deferred for a pure-2D view is worth ~1ms at this scale - do it for correctness/layering, not for performance
decision 4: chunk caching of tile candidates is not needed yet (extraction is 1/50 of submission); revisit at 4x area

open (handed over): Render/Frame self time (4.3/5.0/2.9ms, not monotone in candidates, likely the frame-fence wait) is unattributed by the CPU trace; draw counts are derived from the implementation rule + scene data (no RenderDoc on this machine)
